newsitem.title: FRANCE: French National Front politician fined for racism.
newsitem.headline: French National Front politician fined for racism.

text.p: A senior politician in France's extreme-right National Front was given a six-month suspended prison sentence and fined 50,000 francs ($8,800) on Friday for making racial insults.

A court in Montpellier convicted Bernard Antony, a member of the European Parliament and of the party's national leadership, for remarks he made when a group of African immigrants facing expulsion from France occupied a Paris church last August.

"We should occupy mosques and synagogues since these people occupy our churches. I condemn the emasculated Christians who give shelter to these negroes," Antony had told journalists at the National Front's summer school.
The court ordered him to pay a symbolic one franc (20 cents) in damages to anti-racism associations which had filed lawsuits against him, and to have the judgment published in a local newspaper.

The Movement against Racism and for Friendship among Peoples (MRAP) had filed a complaint for incitement to racial hatred, discrimination, violence and making racial insults. The court accepted only the latter charge.

The National Front, led by anti-immigration crusader Jean-Marie Le Pen, advocates expelling three million immigrants and giving native-born French people priority in jobs, housing and welfare benefits.
